To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the PhoE protein of Escherichio coli is a voltage-gated anion-selective channel in lipid bilayer membrane, that acetylation of lysine residues causes the protein to become cation-selective, and that the selectivity of the native and acetylated proteins is influenced by changes in pH.
the PhoE anion selectivity was increased by chemical acetylation of lysine residues in the protein and that the PhoEs anion selectivity is pH dependent.
chemical modification of the Pho E porin from the outer membrane of Escherichiacoli causes the protein to switch from an anion-selective to a cation-selective channel.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular basis of anion and cation selectivity in the PhoE outer membrane porin.
the chemical modification of the anionic selectivity of the phoE porin.
the molecular basis of ion selectivity of a bacterial porin and has shown that chemical modification of a single porin can alter the selectivity from anion-selective to cation-selective.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the basis of ion selectivity in the PhoE protein is a complex function of the chemical properties of amino acids within or near the channel.
the PhoE channel is a highly pH sensitive cation-selective pore with a fixed number of protonable groups that are titrated by the pH of the solution.
the PhoE channel is anion-selective at low pH and becomes increasingly cation-selective as the pH of the solution bathing the channel increases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the native PhoP PhoR PhoE porins of Escherichiacoli are anion-selective and the acetylated forms of these proteins are cation-selective, that the basis of the anion preference is protonated amino groups in or near the channels and that the anion preference can be altered by changes in pH and/or chemical modification.
anion selectivity is due to fixed positive charges in or near the PhoE pore, whereas cation selectivity is due primarily to deprotonated negative charges.
PhoE porins, which are anion-selective in the absence of acetic anhydryde, are converted to cation-selective porins upon acetylation, and this change in selectivity is reversed by pH changes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the PhoE anion-selective channel can be chemically modified to become cation-selective, and that the basis for the change in selectivity is a change in the ionization of fixed amino acid residues.
the basis of ion selectivity in the PhoE channel is not a simple hydrophobic barrier.
the PhoE channel is a very useful system for studying ion selectivity and that chemical modification of the channel can be used to alter its selectivity.
